findings.text: blocking: _number now returns float(value) where it previously returned the value unchanged, so an integer stays an integer no longer; because _number is the one owner feeding _wall_seconds, the profile's wall_seconds_p90 and odd-count median change type from int to float, and since reckon/ledger.py:2290 writes wall_seconds via int(...), every real profile's p90 renders as "300.0" where it rendered "300"; the rendered state.jinja bytes therefore change, failing the spec requirement that every rendered picker state and every profile figure be unchanged (reproduced: same fixture, base render "p90_s":300, head render "p90_s":300.0).

follow-on: the test that claims to pin an unchanged rendered state renders the new code twice (cold then warm) and asserts equality, so both sides move with the code under test and it passes green over the int-to-float figure change; it guards cache consistency, not the before/after invariance the done_when names.

follow-on: the refactor dropped the ledger._SAFE_ID.fullmatch(project) check that guarded the cache filename (removed from base lane_context.py:268), so the project string now forms the cache leaf unchecked; not reachable today because an unsafe name yields no ledger stamp and the path is never used, but a defence-in-depth check was lost.
